correctness.rationale: For L=F_q h ⊕ U ⊕ Z, dim(U)=dim(Z)=n and [h,u_i]=z_i, an ideal is determined exactly by projection S≤F_qh⊕U, central intersection T≤Z containing [S,V], and a graph map S→Z/T. If S has h component, choose K=S∩U of dimension k and q^{n-k} cosets, T=Z, giving degree n+k+1. If S≤U, k=dim S and j=dim T≥k, the counts are Gaussian(n,k) Gaussian(n-k,j-k) q^{k(n-j)}, degree k+j. Their sum establishes the polynomial including zero and total ideals in every characteristic. Degree of second-class term equals k(n-k)+j(n-j), uniquely maximal at k=j=n/2 for even n, and at three pairs for odd n; first-class degree ≤floor((n+1)^2/4) strictly lower for n≥4. Verified polynomial histograms for n=2,3 q=2, and degree maximizers for n=4..9 independently.
